Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo last week. We have a procurement review this Friday and need a consolidated pricing and packaging view for the compliance/security add-ons you mentioned: audit log retention tiers, KMS/HSM seat vs usage pricing, and geographic residency options (US only + EU). Our main asks: a clear per-month cost breakdown, one-time setup/validation fees, and any volume or term discounts you can offer for a 3-year commitment.

Also important for our legal team: sample contract language around data residency and SOC 2 evidence delivery cadence. Can you send a short proposal and indicate whether you can offer any one-off onboarding credits or trial residency at reduced rate during the first quarter after go-live?

We'd like to get something formal by Thursday EOD if possible.

Best,

Elena — thanks for the clear brief and timeline.

Quick summary of what I'll send by Thursday:
- One-page pricing table for audit log retention (30/90/365/540 days) with per-GB/month and fixed ingestion overhead.
- KMS/HSM options: managed KMS + customer-managed HSM seats (monthly seat + per-request egress), and an alternative per-usage model for smaller volumes.
- Residency: US-only and EU options, with one-time validation fee and optional quarterly attestation.
- Term discounts: single-tier example for 12/24/36-month commitments; we can provide stepped/volume discounts based on committed token volumes.
- Proposal will include two commercial levers: an onboarding credit (one-time) and a monthly credit structure for the first 3 months to offset residency validation costs.

Action for you: confirm whether the EU residency is required at go-live or can be staged after roll-out (this materially impacts the one-time validation lift).

I'll attach a draft SOW and pricing PDF for your legal and procurement teams.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Tessa — quick clarification: our expected monthly token volume for year 1 is ~1.2B tokens, with 60% clinical workloads (high audit-sensitivity). We'd want both audit log retention at 365 days and a HSM-backed KMS for key control.

Two asks from procurement:
1) Can you show a blended per-token cost with the add-ons included vs excluded?
2) Would Redwood consider a one-time onboarding credit to cover residency validation and SOC2 evidence packaging?

If we can get a one-time credit and an illustrative blended rate within procurement's internal target, we can move to the standard PO route quickly.

Thanks,
Carlos

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-23T09:41:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: MedLytics — pricing/credit ask (need approval)

Aditya / Neha — forwarding MedLytics ask. Key points:
- 1.2B tokens expected Y1; wants 365d audit retention + HSM-backed KMS + EU residency optionally staged.
- 1x onboarding credit request (covers residency validation + SOC2 evidence packaging); procurement would move quickly if we provide credit + blended per-token estimate within their target.

Proposed commercial response: offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to 2 months of projected add-on billings (applied as credit on first invoice) + a 10% term discount on add-on list prices for 36-month commit; demonstrate blended per-token with modeled usage.

Question for pricing/leadership: are we comfortable with a 10% term discount plus a credit of that size for a new mid-market account? If needed, can we offer a step-down credit (full for month 1, 50% month 2)?

Also need sign-off for providing sample contract language and committing to quarterly SOC2 evidence deliveries for the first year (we can commit to evidence snapshots, not an audit).

Thanks — need quick reply, procurement expects formal by Thursday.

Best,
Tessa

Tessa — thanks for the context. I’m OK with the commercial posture you proposed with a small adjustment. Thoughts below: 

- Onboarding credit: cap to the equivalent of 1.5 months of projected add-on billings rather than 2 months; that keeps the uplift meaningful but reduces exposure.
- Term discount: 12% on add-ons for a 36-month firm commitment (we can go to 15% if legal confirms auto-renew protections).
- Residencies: charge one-time validation per region, but offer staged validation credits if EU is delayed more than 90 days after US go-live.

We should model blended per-token using the 1.2B figure and show two sensitivity rows (60% clinical, 40% general). I’ll ask pricing ops to produce the blended sheet; Neha can prep the contract language for quarterly attestation delivery.

If you agree, proceed and send to Elena with attachments + a short line that the credit is one-time and will be applied to the first invoice.

Aditya
VP, Revenue Operations

Elena — thanks for your patience; attached is a short pricing proposal and a draft SOW. Summary of commercial points we can confirm now: 

- Audit log retention: 30/90/365/540 days tiers. For your 365-day profile we recommend the mid-volume bracket: $0.045/GB/month ingestion + $0.003/GB/month storage baseline.
- KMS/HSM: two options — managed KMS (no seat) or Customer HSM (seat model). For expected volumes we recommend Customer HSM: $1,500/month/seat + $0.00008 per HSM operation.
- Residency: US-only go-live default. EU residency is available as an add-on; one-time validation fee $12,000/region. If EU is staged >90 days after US go-live we will apply a staged-validation credit of $6,000.
- Term & credits: 12% discount on listed add-on prices for a 36-month firm commitment; one-time onboarding credit capped at 1.5 months of projected add-on billings (applied to first invoice).

Next steps we suggest:
1) Procurement confirms whether EU is required at go-live.
2) If MedLytics agrees to 36-month firm term, we’ll issue a commercial amendment template and a final pricing PDF for signature.
3) Redwood legal will provide the sample residency/SOC2 attestation language for procurement review (Neha included).

I've attached the pricing PDF and SOW draft. Carlos — I’ll follow up with a blended per-token sheet in a separate email today.

Best regards,
Tessa Morgan
